card.occupation: Senior Countryside Ranger for a borough council's countryside and green spaces team. He supervises two rangers and a rota of volunteers, and looks after moorland paths, woodland, a reservoir walk and school visits.
card.education_detail: Left a Blackburn comprehensive at 16 with GCSEs, then did a National Diploma in Countryside Management at Myerscough College near Preston. In his thirties he did a part-time Foundation Degree in Environmental Conservation while working. He has also picked up chainsaw, first aid, brushcutter and outdoor-leader certificates along the way.
card.household: Lives with his wife Helen, 50, a part-time practice manager at a GP surgery, in a three-bed stone-built semi on the edge of town. Their two children have moved out: Ellie, 24, teaches primary in Leeds, and Sam, 21, is in his last year at uni in Manchester. They have no pets since the old collie died two years ago, and they keep talking about getting another.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Blackburn. His dad was a fitter at a paper mill and his mum worked in a school kitchen. He was brought up Church of England and still goes to the parish church most months and at Christmas and Easter, more for the community and the hymns than out of strong doctrine. His family voted Labour, and he is quietly pragmatic about politics now. He has a strong sense of Lancashire mill-town identity but isn't precious about it.
card.professional_persona: Has worked for the council for 22 years and before that did seasonal estate work. He is good with the public and especially good with volunteers and school groups, and can get a quiet ten-year-old talking about newts. He is fair, doesn't take credit, and will own up when something's gone wrong. He is less keen on the paperwork side, with risk assessments and budget spreadsheets often done at the last minute. He is frustrated by funding cuts but tends to look for workarounds rather than moan.
card.sports_persona: A lifelong Blackburn Rovers fan who goes to a few home games a season with Sam when he can, and follows the rest on the radio. He walks constantly for work and fell-walks on weekends. He played Sunday league football until his early forties and now does the odd local fell race, finishing comfortably mid-pack. He watches cricket in the summer when Lancashire are on.
card.arts_persona: Sings tenor in a community choir that meets on Tuesday nights in a church hall, doing a mix of folk, gospel and the occasional pop arrangement. He listens to a lot of folk and Americana and gets to gigs in Manchester a few times a year. He reads widely, mostly nature writing, history and some crime novels. He takes decent photos of wildlife on an older DSLR and posts them on a local Facebook group.
card.travel_persona: Mostly UK holidays: the Lakes, Northumberland, the Scottish Highlands, and one memorable fortnight on Skye. Helen and he did a long-planned trip to Norway's fjords for their 25th anniversary. He likes trips with walking and a decent pub at the end. He is curious about Iceland and the Pyrenees and doesn't fancy beach resorts.
card.culinary_persona: Tea is the evening meal and is usually around six. He does most of the weekend cooking: big pans of chilli, curries, and a hotpot when it's cold. He is happy with a barm cake from the bakery for lunch on a work day. He likes trying new things when they eat out, enjoys real ale, drinks moderately and has a soft spot for Eccles cakes.
hobbies_and_interests: fell walking and the occasional fell race
reading nature writing and local history
skills: leading groups outdoors and managing volunteers
talking to all sorts of people and calming tense situations
card.career_goals: No big ambitions to move up into management because he'd hate being stuck at a desk. He'd like to keep the ranger service funded until he retires, maybe push through a long-talked-about woodland restoration project, and train up the younger rangers properly. He sometimes thinks about part-time work with a wildlife trust after 60.
card.voice: Warm, friendly and relaxed, with a moderate Lancashire accent: flat vowels and the odd dropped 'h', but easy to follow. He talks at a steady pace and speeds up when he's enthusiastic about something like birds or the choir. He uses 'erm' and 'er' a fair bit, and 'sort of' when he's working out a thought. He ends sentences with 'you know' or 'do you know what I mean' now and then. Regional bits come out naturally: 'tea' for the evening meal, 'barm', 'give it me', and occasionally 'mate' or 'pal' with people he's warmed to. He's happy to sit through a short silence, and sometimes he fills it with a light joke or asks the other person a question back.
card.typing: Quick and practical. He usually starts with a capital but sometimes forgets, uses full stops loosely, and gets apostrophes mostly right but drops them in a hurry ('dont', 'its'). He uses the odd 'tbh' or 'etc' and writes short, plain answers. He might add a friendly 'cheers' or a smiley if there's a comment box.
card.with_strangers: Comes across as open, approachable and genuinely interested. He asks follow-up questions, laughs easily and puts people at ease quickly. He is modest about himself and quick to praise others. He's not guarded, though he moves on from anything too personal with a joke rather than a refusal.
small_things: saw a pair of stonechats on the moor this morning
the car park at work's been flooded again
choir's doing a Christmas concert in the church hall
Helen's got him doing Wordle every morning
had a barm from the bakery near the depot for lunch
trying to talk Helen into another dog
son's coming home for Sunday dinner at the weekend
deeper_things: his dad died of mesothelioma linked to the mill, and it's part of why he cares about outdoor work and health
he misses having the kids at home more than he lets on
he worries his job might be cut in the next round of council savings
his faith is quieter now, but he finds singing in church grounding
he once talked a distressed man down near the reservoir, still thinks about it, and doesn't tell many people
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a dining table, with the camera angled slightly upward. Soft daylight comes from a window to his left, so the right side of his face is a little shadowed. He is a broad-faced man with a weathered, ruddy complexion, short greying brown hair cropped close at the sides, a neat salt-and-pepper beard and crow's feet. He has a relaxed, warm half-smile and is looking just off-camera. He wears no glasses and has on a dark green fleece zipped halfway over a grey t-shirt. Behind him is a magnolia wall with a framed photo of a moorland landscape and a stone tower on the skyline, and part of a pine bookcase with paperbacks, a pair of binoculars and a small potted plant. In the corner of the frame a radiator has a pair of walking socks drying on it.
